assessment: Gao et al. developed various genetic permutations of mouse models of kindlin-2 deficiency in the hepatocytes to decipher its role. Hepatocyte-specific loss of kindlin-2 resulted in severe inflammatory liver injury, accelerated fibrosis/portal hypertension, and massive hepatocyte cell death by apoptosis. These effects are reversed by ablation of TNF signally or by caspase 8 deletion. AAV-mediated replacement of kindlin-2 protects the mice from chemically induced acute liver injury. Together the findings are novel with significant translational potential.
